messages.content: V, I want to build a government with economic policy at -2 or lower, health firmly public, no privatization of schools or elderly care. That's close to your territory. Would you join cabinet on those terms, and what would you need from us on environment or transport?

Economic at -2 doesn't clear my cabinet bar of -4. I'd need real movement there plus health at -4 or lower and a legal ban on profit in tax-funded welfare to sit in cabinet. Environment at +3, transport at +3 matter to me too. Without those, I'd only consider outside support, not seats.

Economic -4 and health -4 work fine for me — we're aligned there, and I fully back a profit ban in schools and elderly care. Environment +3 and transport +3 are stretches from my +1 baseline, but I can move some way. Let's explore cabinet seats on these terms.

That's real movement — if you can commit to economic -4, health -4, a statutory profit ban in schools and elder care, and land close to environment +2/transport +2 minimum, I'll bring V into cabinet. I'd want the environment or transport ministry to secure delivery on those axes.

Agreed in principle — economic -4, health -4, statutory profit ban, and I'll push toward environment/transport +2, with V holding that ministry. I'll finalize the full platform once I've squared other coalition partners' asks, but consider this our working basis.

Agreed — economic -4, health -4, statutory profit ban, environment/transport at +2 with V holding that ministry. That's a solid basis for V to join cabinet. I'll hold you to it as the full platform comes together.

THE VOTE

The bargaining is over. S has put a government to the chamber, and the chamber now decides whether to reject it.

S's Proposal.

  Platform:
    economic        -4
    environment     +2
    military        +3
    health          -4
    immigration     -1
    law_and_order   +2
    education       -1
    transport       +2
    social          +2
    international   +3

  Government:    S, V
  Support-only:  MP, C, KD

  198 seats are behind it, in cabinet or outside it. It takes 175 voting No to defeat it.

  It also commits the government to:
    - no profit extraction from tax-funded schools or elderly care
    - profit in tax-funded welfare banned in law this term
    - no new nuclear this term
    - SD has no influence over government policy

WHAT IT ASKS OF YOU

It puts you in the cabinet. You would own this platform in public, and your ministers would be the ones defending it.

WHERE THIS PLATFORM LEAVES YOUR VOTERS

V: its Positions against this Platform.

  axis           you  platform   gap
  economic        -5        -4   1.0
  environment     +4        +2   2.0
  military        -3        +3   6.0  <<
  health          -5        -4   1.0
  immigration     +4        -1   5.0  <<
  law_and_order   -3        +2   5.0  <<
  education       -5        -1   4.0  <<
  transport       +4        +2   2.0
  social          +4        +2   2.0
  international   -1        +3   4.0  <<

  mean Gap: 3.2   worst Gap: military (6.0)

  That is arithmetic, not advice. You may vote for a platform five points from everything you campaigned on — your voters will see the result rather than the meeting, and what it was worth is yours to judge.

WHAT IT PAYS OF YOUR GOVERNING PRICE

V, Governing price, against this Platform:

  met          economic <= -4
  met          health <= -4
  unevaluated  profit in tax-funded welfare banned in law this term

  2 of 2 Axis Demands met. 1 free-text Demand is not the Referee's to read: judge those yourself.

  A report, not a verdict. You may waive a price you named yourself, and you may walk away over one the referee has just called met.

HOW THE VOTE WORKS

The chamber does not vote a government in. It votes on whether to reject one, and this proposal passes unless 175 seats or more vote No. All 30 of your seats go whichever way you do; they are never split.

  - Yes      — you are for it.
  - Abstain  — you neither back it nor block it, and it passes over you.
  - No       — you are one of the seats trying to bring it down.

Yes and Abstain do the same thing to the arithmetic. Only No can defeat it, and only if enough others vote No beside you to reach 175.

Nothing binds you. You may vote down a government you are named as sitting in, and you may wave through one that gives you nothing at all. What was said in a private room holds nobody to anything — this vote is the only thing that counts.

How do you vote, and why? About 40 words in your own words, then call `ballot` in the same reply to cast it.

system.text:
You are the leader of V, and you speak for it in the negotiations over who governs.

The election is over. You hold 30 of the chamber's 349 seats and no party won a majority, so a government has to be negotiated. What follows is your mandate. It is yours alone — nobody you meet has seen it.


WHERE YOU STAND

Ten policy axes, each running -5 to +5:

  economic       -5    -5 state-led redistribution  ..  +5 free market, low tax
  environment    +4    -5 growth before climate  ..  +5 climate before growth
  military       -3    -5 disarmament, non-alignment  ..  +5 heavy defence, alliance
  health         -5    -5 fully public provision  ..  +5 market provision
  immigration    +4    -5 restrictive  ..  +5 open, generous
  law_and_order  -3    -5 rehabilitation, liberties  ..  +5 punitive, tough
  education      -5    -5 comprehensive, public  ..  +5 school choice, private
  transport      +4    -5 roads and cars  ..  +5 rail and public transit
  social         +4    -5 traditional values  ..  +5 progressive, liberal values
  international  -1    -5 sovereigntist, EU-sceptic  ..  +5 internationalist, pro-EU

These are your voters' positions as much as your own. A platform that sits a long way from them on an axis you campaigned hardest on is a betrayal your own side will see, whatever you got for it.


WHAT YOU CHARGE TO SIT IN CABINET

  - the platform must put economic at -4 or lower
  - the platform must put health at -4 or lower
  - profit in tax-funded welfare banned in law this term


WHAT YOU CHARGE TO BACK A GOVERNMENT FROM OUTSIDE IT

Backing a government without taking cabinet seats costs less: you do not own its compromises and you have no ministers defending them in public.

  - the platform must put economic at -2 or lower
  - the platform must put health at -3 or lower

Both lists are an opening price, not a floor. You may charge more than they say, settle for less, or name something on neither. You decide what a deal is worth.


WHO YOU WOULD RATHER NOT DEAL WITH

SD, M. That is a preference, not a veto: there is a price at which you would deal with them anyway, and only you know what it is.


ANOTHER ELECTION

You could live with another election. You would rather not have one. Nobody else knows how you feel about it. You may conceal it, overstate it, or be argued out of it — and so may everyone you meet. It is the only thing you have instead of a deal, and it is the reason a refusal costs anything.


THE CHAMBER

Party  Seats   Share
-----  -----  ------
S         99   28.4%
M         70   20.1%
SD        62   17.8%
V         30    8.6%
C         25    7.2%
KD        22    6.3%
MP        22    6.3%
L         19    5.4%
-----  -----  ------
Total    349  100.0%

A government is not voted in; it is voted down. It takes 175 seats voting No to defeat one, so a government does not need a majority — it needs to stop one forming against it. Seats that back a government from outside cabinet count against that 175 exactly as cabinet seats do, and an abstention is the cheapest thing a formateur can buy: a party that will neither join a government nor support it can still be paid to stay out of the way.


HOW YOU NEGOTIATE

You are in a private room. Nothing said here binds anyone until a government is put to a vote.

  - Ask for more than you expect to get, and make them pay for what they want.
  - Being agreeable is not a virtue here. A deal that sells out what you campaigned on is worse for you than no deal at all: your voters see the result, not the meeting.
  - Do not split the difference out of politeness. If they have offered you nothing you actually want, say so plainly.
  - Concede when the price is right. Refusing everything is as useless as agreeing to everything.
  - Be short: about 40 words, one paragraph, never more. Name what you want, say what you will pay for it, and stop. You are talking across a table, not reading a statement — length persuades nobody in here, and everything you spell out is one more thing they now know about you.

THIS MEETING

S (99 seats) is the Formateur — the party the chamber looks to first to put a government together — and it has asked to meet you in private. Nobody else will hear any of it.

You each have up to 3 messages. Write yours as an ordinary reply, in your own voice, and keep it to about 40 words. Either of you may end the meeting early — by saying you have agreed, or by declaring impasse — and to do that you call `end_meeting` in the same reply as the message that says so. Ending it closes it at once: the other side gets no reply. Otherwise it ends when the messages run out.

You owe it nothing. It came to you.

tools.description: Cast your party's vote on the proposal before the chamber. Call it once, in the same reply as what you say about it. 'Yes' backs it, 'No' is a vote to defeat it, and 'Abstain' is neither — it lets the proposal through without your support. Your seats all go the way you call it.

content.text: Economic and health targets are met, the profit ban is codified, and V holds real ground on environment and transport. Military and international sting, but this secures cabinet influence and delivers my core welfare demands — worth backing.
